title: Conditional connectors: 如果, 只要, 只有, 除非
titleHanzi: 如果 / 只要 / 只有 / 除非
summary: These words open the condition clause. Each one signals a different kind of condition: a plain 'if', a sufficient condition, the only condition that works, and an exception.
pattern: 如果 + condition, (就) + result  ·  只要 + condition, 就 + result  ·  只有 + condition, 才 + result  ·  除非 + condition, 才 / 不 + result

rules.rule: **如果 is the plain 'if'.** It sets up an open or hypothetical condition. In longer sentences the result clause usually starts with 就 ('then'); in short ones 就 can be left out.

examples.hanzi: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去公园。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ míngtiān xiàyǔ, wǒmen jiù bú qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: If it rains tomorrow, we will not go to the park.

examples.hanzi: 如果你累了，就早点休息。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ lèi le, jiù zǎodiǎn xiūxi.
examples.english: If you are tired, rest early.

examples.hanzi: 如果有问题，可以随时问我。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ yǒu wèntí, kěyǐ suíshí wèn wǒ.
examples.english: If you have questions, you can ask me at any time.

rules.rule: **只要 means 'as long as'.** It says that one condition is enough to bring about the result. Nothing else is needed, so the tone is confident. The result clause takes 就.

examples.hanzi: 只要你努力，就一定能学好汉语。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào nǐ nǔlì, jiù yídìng néng xuéhǎo Hànyǔ.
examples.english: As long as you work hard, you will definitely be able to learn Chinese well.

examples.hanzi: 只要不下雨，我们就去爬山。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào bú xiàyǔ, wǒmen jiù qù páshān.
examples.english: As long as it does not rain, we will go hiking.

rules.rule: **只有 means 'only if'.** The condition is necessary and the only way to the result. Its partner in the result clause is 才 ('only then').

examples.hanzi: 只有多练习，才能说得流利。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu duō liànxí, cái néng shuō de liúlì.
examples.english: Only with more practice can you speak fluently.

examples.hanzi: 只有老师同意，你才可以请假。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu lǎoshī tóngyì, nǐ cái kěyǐ qǐngjià.
examples.english: Only if the teacher agrees can you ask for leave.

rules.rule: **除非 = unless, the one exception.** It names the only condition under which the result changes. The main clause is usually negative (不会, 不能) or uses 才 for 'only then'.

examples.hanzi: 除非你道歉，他不会原谅你。
examples.pinyin: Chúfēi nǐ dàoqiàn, tā bú huì yuánliàng nǐ.
examples.english: Unless you apologize, he will not forgive you.

examples.hanzi: 除非天气变好，我们才出去。
examples.pinyin: Chúfēi tiānqì biànhǎo, wǒmen cái chūqu.
examples.english: We will go out only if the weather improves.

examples.hanzi: 没有别的办法，除非你自己去。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu biéde bànfǎ, chúfēi nǐ zìjǐ qù.
examples.english: There is no other way, except for you going yourself.

contrasts.text: 如果 is a neutral 'if'. 只要 says the condition is enough on its own, so it sounds stronger and more certain.
只要 gives a sufficient condition (any one of them works); 只有 gives the necessary condition (nothing else works), and it normally pairs with 才.

pitfalls: ✗ 只有你努力，就能成功。 → ✓ 只要你努力，就能成功。 Use 只要 for 'as long as'. 只有 means that this is the only route, so it needs 才 in the result.
✗ 除非你不来，我就去。 → ✓ 除非你来，我才去。 Do not put a negative in the 除非 clause just because 'unless' is negative in English; the condition itself is positive.
✗ 只要明天下雨了，我们不去。 → ✓ 如果明天下雨，我们不去。 For a plain hypothetical use 如果; 只要 suggests that this single condition decides the outcome.

title: Concessive connectors: 虽然, 即使, 尽管, 无论
titleHanzi: 虽然 / 即使 / 尽管 / 无论
summary: Concessive connectors admit a point and then say that the result still holds. 虽然 and 尽管 deal with facts, 即使 with hypotheticals, and 无论 with a whole range of cases.
pattern: 虽然 + fact, 但是 + result  ·  即使 + hypothesis, 也 + result  ·  尽管 + fact, 还是 + result  ·  无论 / 不管 + variable, 都 + result

rules.rule: **虽然 … 但是 (可是) = although … but.** It states a real fact and then contrasts it with the result. Either half can be used alone in short speech, but the pair is standard in writing.

examples.hanzi: 虽然天气很冷，但是我们还是去了公园。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán tiānqì hěn lěng, dànshì wǒmen háishi qù le gōngyuán.
examples.english: Although the weather was very cold, we still went to the park.

examples.hanzi: 虽然他年纪小，但是很懂事。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán tā niánjì xiǎo, dànshì hěn dǒngshì.
examples.english: Although he is young, he is very sensible.

examples.hanzi: 虽然我很忙，可是我每天都学习汉语。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán wǒ hěn máng, kěshì wǒ měi tiān dōu xuéxí Hànyǔ.
examples.english: Although I am very busy, I study Chinese every day.

rules.rule: **即使 … 也 = even if.** It takes a hypothetical or extreme case and says the result still holds. The main clause usually has 也 or 还是; the situation is not a known fact.

examples.hanzi: 即使下大雨，我也要去上班。
examples.pinyin: Jíshǐ xià dàyǔ, wǒ yě yào qù shàngbān.
examples.english: Even if it rains heavily, I still have to go to work.

examples.hanzi: 即使你不同意，我也会坚持。
examples.pinyin: Jíshǐ nǐ bù tóngyì, wǒ yě huì jiānchí.
examples.english: Even if you disagree, I will still stick to it.

rules.rule: **尽管 … 还是 / 仍然 = despite.** The difficulty is a known fact, and the result happens anyway. It sounds more emphatic and formal than 虽然, and the main clause often uses 还是 or 仍然.

examples.hanzi: 尽管很贵，他还是买了那辆车。
examples.pinyin: Jǐnguǎn hěn guì, tā háishi mǎi le nà liàng chē.
examples.english: Despite the high price, he still bought that car.

examples.hanzi: 尽管困难很多，我们仍然坚持下来了。
examples.pinyin: Jǐnguǎn kùnnan hěn duō, wǒmen réngrán jiānchí xiàlai le.
examples.english: Despite many difficulties, we still kept going.

rules.rule: **无论 / 不管 … 都 = no matter what.** The first half has a variable: a question word (谁, 什么), a 'whether or not' pair, or an 'A or B' pair. The second half says that the result is the same in every case.

examples.hanzi: 无论刮风还是下雨，他都骑自行车上班。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn guāfēng háishi xiàyǔ, tā dōu qí zìxíngchē shàngbān.
examples.english: Whether it is windy or rainy, he rides his bike to work.

examples.hanzi: 不管谁来，我们都欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn shéi lái, wǒmen dōu huānyíng.
examples.english: No matter who comes, we welcome them.

examples.hanzi: 无论什么问题，他都能解决。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn shénme wèntí, tā dōu néng jiějué.
examples.english: Whatever the problem, he can solve it.

contrasts.text: 虽然 takes a fact that is true (he is old); 即使 takes a hypothesis (even if he were old). Choose by whether the condition is real.
The two are close in meaning. 尽管 is more emphatic and often pairs with 还是 or 仍然 in the main clause.
无论 covers every case in a set (who, what, whether); 即使 picks one extreme case and says the result still holds there.

pitfalls: ✗ 虽然下雨，所以我们不去。 → ✓ 因为下雨，所以我们不去。 虽然 introduces a concession (despite), not a cause; 所以 is a causal word and does not fit here.
✗ 即使他年纪大，他很健康。 → ✓ 虽然他年纪大，但是很健康。 即使 is for hypotheticals. When the fact is already known (he is old), use 虽然.
✗ 无论他来，我们都高兴。 → ✓ 无论他来不来，我们都高兴。 无论 needs a variable: a question word, a 'whether or not' pair or an 'A or B' pair. A single fixed condition does not work.

title: Causal connectors: 因为, 由于, 既然
titleHanzi: 因为 / 由于 / 既然
summary: These words give a reason. 因为 states a plain cause, 由于 does the same in formal writing, and 既然 uses a reason that both sides already accept as true.
pattern: 因为 + cause, (所以) + result  ·  由于 + cause (written), + result  ·  既然 + known fact, 就 + conclusion

rules.rule: **因为 … 所以 = because … so.** This is the everyday cause-and-result pair. Either half can be left out: 因为 alone is the natural answer to 为什么, and 所以 alone works when the cause is already clear.

examples.hanzi: 因为下雨，所以我们没去公园。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xiàyǔ, suǒyǐ wǒmen méi qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: Because it rained, we did not go to the park.

examples.hanzi: 我迟到了，因为公交车坏了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chídào le, yīnwèi gōngjiāochē huài le.
examples.english: I was late because the bus broke down.

examples.hanzi: 因为他生病，所以没来上课。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi tā shēngbìng, suǒyǐ méi lái shàngkè.
examples.english: Because he was ill, he did not come to class.

rules.rule: **因为 in a short answer.** To answer 为什么, say 因为 and then the reason. It works without 所以 and is the normal form in speech.

examples.hanzi: 你为什么不吃饭？因为我不饿。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wèishénme bù chī fàn? Yīnwèi wǒ bú è.
examples.english: Why are you not eating? Because I am not hungry.

examples.hanzi: 你为什么学汉语？因为我喜欢中国文化。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wèishénme xué Hànyǔ? Yīnwèi wǒ xǐhuan Zhōngguó wénhuà.
examples.english: Why are you learning Chinese? Because I like Chinese culture.

rules.rule: **由于 = due to.** It is a formal, written cause word and is usually followed by a noun phrase or a clause describing the cause. It sounds official, so it appears in reports and announcements.

examples.hanzi: 由于天气原因，航班取消了。
examples.pinyin: Yóuyú tiānqì yuányīn, hángbān qǔxiāo le.
examples.english: Due to the weather, the flight was cancelled.

examples.hanzi: 由于工作需要，他经常出差。
examples.pinyin: Yóuyú gōngzuò xūyào, tā jīngcháng chūchāi.
examples.english: Because of work requirements, he often travels on business.

rules.rule: **既然 … 就 = since (as things are).** The cause is something both speakers already accept, and the conclusion follows from it. It is used to draw a decision or a suggestion from a known fact, not to give a new reason.

examples.hanzi: 既然你已经决定了，我们就支持你。
examples.pinyin: Jìrán nǐ yǐjīng juédìng le, wǒmen jiù zhīchí nǐ.
examples.english: Since you have already decided, we will support you.

examples.hanzi: 既然大家都同意，那就这样定吧。
examples.pinyin: Jìrán dàjiā dōu tóngyì, nà jiù zhèyàng dìng ba.
examples.english: Since everyone agrees, let's settle it like this.

contrasts.text: Same meaning. 由于 is formal and written and often sits at the start of a sentence; 因为 is the everyday word.
因为 introduces a new reason the listener may not know. 既然 presents a reason that is already shared, and the result is a conclusion or suggestion.

pitfalls: ✗ 因为很累，但是他还是去了。 → ✓ 虽然很累，但是他还是去了。 因为 gives a cause (the result follows from it); 虽然 gives a concession (the result is unexpected). Mixing them changes the logic.
✗ 由于我生病，我请假了。 → ✓ 因为我生病，我请假了。 由于 is formal and written; in everyday speech 因为 is the natural choice.
✗ 既然我不知道，你告诉我。 → ✓ 因为我不知道，你告诉我。 既然 needs a fact that both sides already accept. If you are only giving a new reason, use 因为.

title: Contrast and addition: 但是, 然而, 不过, 不但 … 而且, 甚至
titleHanzi: 但是 / 然而 / 不过 / 不但 … 而且 / 甚至
summary: This group covers the 'but' words, the 'not only … but also' pair for adding a stronger point, and 甚至 for the extreme case that is 'even'.
pattern: A, 但是 / 不过 / 然而 B  ·  不但 A, 而且 B  ·  甚至 + extreme case

rules.rule: **但是 / 可是 / 不过 = but.** 但是 is the neutral word. 不过 is softer and often follows a compliment ('it is good, but …'). Use only one contrast word per contrast.

examples.hanzi: 这个饭馆很好，但是有点贵。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fànguǎn hěn hǎo, dànshì yǒudiǎn guì.
examples.english: This restaurant is very good, but it is a bit expensive.

examples.hanzi: 他想去，可是没有时间。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng qù, kěshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
examples.english: He wants to go, but he has no time.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服不错，不过太大了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu búcuò, búguò tài dà le.
examples.english: This piece of clothing is nice, but it is too big.

rules.rule: **然而 = however.** It is a written, formal word. It usually starts a new sentence (after a full stop) and is followed by a comma, so it reads as a turn in the argument.

examples.hanzi: 他很努力。然而，成绩并不理想。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn nǔlì. Rán'ér, chéngjì bìng bù lǐxiǎng.
examples.english: He worked hard. However, his results were not ideal.

examples.hanzi: 计划很好。然而，执行起来很难。
examples.pinyin: Jìhuà hěn hǎo. Rán'ér, zhíxíng qǐlai hěn nán.
examples.english: The plan is good. However, carrying it out is very hard.

rules.rule: **不但 … 而且 = not only … but also.** The second half adds a stronger or additional point. 不但 comes first and 而且 must follow to complete the pattern; 也 can replace 而且 in some sentences.

examples.hanzi: 她不但会说汉语，而且会写汉字。
examples.pinyin: Tā búdàn huì shuō Hànyǔ, érqiě huì xiě Hànzì.
examples.english: She not only speaks Chinese, but also writes Chinese characters.

examples.hanzi: 这家店不但便宜，而且东西很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn búdàn piányi, érqiě dōngxi hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This shop is not only cheap, but the goods are also very good.

examples.hanzi: 他不但迟到了，而且没有道歉。
examples.pinyin: Tā búdàn chídào le, érqiě méiyǒu dàoqiàn.
examples.english: Not only was he late, but he also did not apologize.

rules.rule: **甚至 = even (the extreme case).** It picks the most surprising example to show how strong a point is. It is different from 而且, which only adds another fact.

examples.hanzi: 他忙得甚至没有时间吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Tā máng de shènzhì méiyǒu shíjiān chīfàn.
examples.english: He is so busy that he does not even have time to eat.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题很简单，甚至小孩子都会。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí hěn jiǎndān, shènzhì xiǎoháizi dōu huì.
examples.english: This question is so simple that even children can do it.

contrasts.text: 但是 joins two clauses in ordinary speech; 然而 is written and usually begins a new sentence, adding a note of reflection.
而且 adds a second, equally important fact. 甚至 picks the extreme example, the one that makes the point surprising.

pitfalls: ✗ 这个很好，但是不过太贵了。 → ✓ 这个很好，不过太贵了。 Do not stack contrast words: use one of 但是, 不过 or 然而 for each contrast.
✗ 他很聪明，甚至他很努力。 → ✓ 他很聪明，而且很努力。 甚至 marks an extreme case, not a simple addition. When you are only adding a second fact, use 而且.
✗ 他很聪明，不但很努力。 → ✓ 他不但很聪明，而且很努力。 不但 needs its partner 而且 (or 也) later in the sentence; on its own it leaves the sentence unfinished.

title: Choice, sequence and 'otherwise': 或者, 还是, 先 … 然后, 否则
titleHanzi: 或者 / 还是 / 先…然后 / 否则
summary: These connectors offer options, order actions, and warn about consequences. The main split is that 或者 is for statements and 还是 for questions.
pattern: A 或者 B（statement）  ·  A 还是 B？（question）  ·  先 A，然后 B  ·  A，否则 / 要不然 + consequence

rules.rule: **或者 = or, in statements.** It offers alternatives in a declarative sentence, often about plans or possibilities.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们可以去爬山，或者在家休息。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen kěyǐ qù páshān, huòzhě zài jiā xiūxi.
examples.english: On the weekend we can go hiking, or rest at home.

examples.hanzi: 我们可以坐火车，或者开车去。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kěyǐ zuò huǒchē, huòzhě kāichē qù.
examples.english: We can go by train, or drive there.

rules.rule: **还是 = or, in questions.** When you ask someone to choose between two options, use 还是. 或者 in the same question sounds less natural.

examples.hanzi: 你明天来还是后天来？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ míngtiān lái háishi hòutiān lái?
examples.english: Are you coming tomorrow or the day after?

examples.hanzi: 我们坐地铁还是打车？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò dìtiě háishi dǎchē?
examples.english: Shall we take the subway or a taxi?

rules.rule: **先 … 然后 = first … then.** 先 marks the first step, and 然后 the next one. Use them to show a clear order in which things happen.

examples.hanzi: 我们先吃饭，然后去看电影。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān chīfàn, ránhòu qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: We will eat first, and then go to see a film.

examples.hanzi: 先写作业，然后再玩儿。
examples.pinyin: Xiān xiě zuòyè, ránhòu zài wánr.
examples.english: Do your homework first, and then play.

rules.rule: **否则 / 要不然 = otherwise, or else.** The second clause states the consequence if the first clause is not done. 否则 is written; 要不然 is the more colloquial word with the same meaning.

examples.hanzi: 你应该快点，否则会迟到。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi kuàidiǎn, fǒuzé huì chídào.
examples.english: You should hurry, otherwise you will be late.

examples.hanzi: 要赶紧走，要不然赶不上火车了。
examples.pinyin: Yào gǎnjǐn zǒu, yàobùrán gǎn bu shàng huǒchē le.
examples.english: We must leave quickly, otherwise we will miss the train.

examples.hanzi: 多穿衣服，要不然会感冒。
examples.pinyin: Duō chuān yīfu, yàobùrán huì gǎnmào.
examples.english: Wear more clothes, otherwise you will catch a cold.

contrasts.text: 或者 is for statements that offer alternatives; 还是 is for questions that ask the listener to choose.
Same meaning. 否则 is formal and written; 要不然 is everyday speech.

pitfalls: ✗ 你来或者不来？ → ✓ 你来还是不来？ In a question about a choice, use 还是 (or the A-not-A form), not 或者.
✗ 我吃饭以后，然后去。 → ✓ 我先吃饭，然后去。 Use 先 or 以后 with 然后, not both, when you mark the order.
✗ 快点，否则你迟到了。 → ✓ 快点，否则你会迟到。 否则 introduces a possible future consequence, so the result usually takes 会 or 就要.
